## 1\. Uniform normal ellipticity all the way to the simplex boundary

Let

\[
\Sigma_N=\{c\in[0,1]^N:\sum_i c_i=1\},\qquad
E=\{J\in\mathbb R^N:\sum_iJ_i=0\}.
\]

Define the constrained friction operator

\[
(\mathcal B(c)J)_i
=\sum_{j\ne i}f_{ij}(c_jJ_i-c_iJ_j).
\]

The constitutive equations become

\[
\mathcal B(c)J=-\nabla c.
\]

Write \(f_-=\min_{i\ne j}f_{ij}\) and \(f_+=\max_{i\ne j}f_{ij}\)\.

For an interior composition \(c_i>0\), use the inner product

\[
\langle J,Z\rangle_{c^{-1}}
=\sum_i\frac{J_iZ_i}{c_i}.
\]

The operator \(\mathcal B(c)\) is self-adjoint in this metric on \(E\), and

\[
\begin{aligned}
\langle J,\mathcal B(c)J\rangle_{c^{-1}}
&=\frac12\sum_{i,j}f_{ij}c_ic_j
\left|\frac{J_i}{c_i}-\frac{J_j}{c_j}\right|^2\\
&\in
\left[
f_-\sum_i\frac{J_i^2}{c_i},
f_+\sum_i\frac{J_i^2}{c_i}
\right].
\end{aligned}
\]

Therefore

\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{spec}(\mathcal B(c)|_E)
\subset[f_-,f_+].
}
\tag{1}
\]

The entries of \(\mathcal B(c)\) depend continuously on \(c\)\. Passing to the boundary gives the same spectral inclusion for every \(c\in\Sigma_N\), including pure-species vertices.

Thus the reduced diffusion operator

\[
D(c)=\big(\mathcal B(c)|_E\big)^{-1}
\]

exists everywhere on the closed simplex and satisfies

\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{spec}D(c)
\subset[1/f_+,1/f_-].
}
\tag{2}
\]

In particular, the problem does not lose normal ellipticity when an individual species concentration reaches zero.

This is a spectral statement, not a claim that the generally nonsymmetric reduced diffusion matrix is positive definite in the ordinary Euclidean quadratic form.

## 2\. An explicit algebraic representation valid at zero concentrations

Set \(d=N-1\), eliminate \(c_N\) and \(J_N\), and write \(y=(c_1,\ldots,c_d)\)\. Define

\[
a_i(c)=\sum_{j\ne i}f_{ij}c_j.
\]

The reduced friction matrix is

\[
M_{ik}(c)
=
\delta_{ik}a_i(c)
-c_if_{ik}+c_if_{iN},
\qquad 1\leq i,k\leq d,
\]

where \(f_{ii}=0\) for this formula.

The system becomes

\[
\boxed{
\partial_t y+b\cdot\nabla y
=\nabla\cdot\big(M(c)^{-1}\nabla y\big).
}
\tag{3}
\]

From (1),

\[
\det M(c)\geq f_-^d.
\]

Consequently, every coefficient of \(M(c)^{-1}\) is a rational function of \(c\) whose denominator is uniformly separated from zero on the closed simplex.

## 5\. An unconditional global weak homogenization theorem

The preceding structural results allow a further extension of the accepted entropy controller.

For every smooth divergence-free prescribed velocity, the bounded-weak-solution construction of Jüngel–Stelzer can be adapted to the transport term.

The main points are as follows.

First, use entropy variables for the regularized system and an implicit time discretization. If \(h(c)=\sum_i c_i\log c_i\), testing by the entropy variables produces the additional transport contribution

\[
\int_{\mathbb T^3}b\cdot\nabla c\cdot\nabla_c h(c)\,dx
=
\int_{\mathbb T^3}b\cdot\nabla h(c)\,dx=0.
\]

Thus the smooth stationary incompressible transport does not alter the discrete entropy estimate.

Second, the entropy-variable construction preserves the simplex constraint. The original compactness argument supplies the concentration-gradient bounds. The added term \(\nabla\cdot(bc)\) is bounded in the same negative Sobolev space needed for time compactness.

Third, the matrix inverse constructed in Section 2 extends continuously to the closed simplex. It permits the limiting fluxes to satisfy the Maxwell–Stefan relations even where some concentrations vanish.

The weak existence argument therefore produces global entropy-admissible solutions with

\[
\begin{gathered}
0\leq c_i\leq1,\qquad \sum_i c_i=1,\\
c_i\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}([0,\infty);H^1(\mathbb T^3)),\\
J_i\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}([0,\infty);L^2(\mathbb T^3)),\\
\partial_t c_i\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}([0,\infty);H^{-1}(\mathbb T^3)).
\end{gathered}
\]

This follows the entropy discretization and compactness machinery of Jüngel–Stelzer rather than a strong regularity theorem. citeturn621759view2
